subject: pol-dy
title: POL.DY.------PROG.CONT.
description: Diagram in CMOA(II)-3 (Creative Music Outside of America, Level One — France/Italy/Northern Europe/Japan), first of two on book p245. Opens Braxton's chapter argument: 'the planet expansion of post-Parker creativity can be viewed as related to the social-reality implications of the Second World War — and the subsequent interest (focus) on creative black music that solidified in that period profoundly affected the vibrational creative arena of both western Europe and Japan.' (C)POL-DY (the concept of political dynamics) is crossed with PROG-CONT (progressional continuance): the question is what political-dynamics produces when crossed with progressional-continuance — the political-dynamics here being the post-WW2 reordering that opened European and Japanese receptivity to creative black music. (R)INFO-DY (reality of information dynamics) feeds into the central axis from the upper-left. RIT-DY (ritual dynamics) and SPT-DY (spectacle dynamics) form the upper-center cluster. PROG-CONT sits at the upper-right. CULT-INFO-DY (culture-information dynamics) anchors the upper-right output. INFO-DE (information descent) sits below the crossing. SOC-RT-DY (social-reality dynamics) feeds in from the lower-left. AFL (affinity alignment) sits centrally. PART (participation) anchors the lower-center. AF-DY (affinity dynamics) and APP-RDEF (apparent redefinition) form the lower-right cluster. Structural argument: political-dynamics-as-concept crossed with progressional-continuance is mediated by ritual-dynamics and spectacle-dynamics in the upper register (these two compete for the meaning of post-war reordering) and information-descent in the lower register. The diagram exposes Braxton's structural commitment: the post-Parker spread to Europe/Japan happened through political-dynamics, but ritual-dynamics versus spectacle-dynamics is the live argument — the productive output (culture-information-dynamics, affinity-dynamics) registers only if ritual-dynamics wins; otherwise the crossing produces apparent-redefinition instead.
